For a graph with girth g ≥ 2k (even) and minimum degree δ, the number of vertices must satisfy n ≥ 2·∑_{i=0}^{k-1} (δ-1)^i. For girth ≥ 8 (k=4) and minimum degree δ=4: n ≥ 2·(1 + 3 + 9 + 27) = 2·40 = 80. With only 18 vertices, this is impossible. The argument: pick any edge (u,v); the BFS trees rooted at u and v (each of depth k-1=3, excluding the edge uv) must be completely disjoint and internally non-overlapping (any shared vertex would create a cycle shorter than 8). Each tree has at least 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 = 40 distinct vertices, requiring at least 80 total vertices. Since 18 << 80, no graph on 18 vertices can simultaneously have girth ≥ 8 and every vertex with degree ≥ 4.
